source_metadata.title: Evaluation of unfractionated heparin therapy for venous thromboembolism using adjusted body weight in elderly or higher weight patients

atoms.canonical_statement: The study compared adjusted-body-weight–based versus total-body-weight–based UFH initiation in older adults and/or patients with higher body weight treated for suspected or confirmed VTE, with time to first therapeutic anti-Xa as the principal efficacy outcome.
This was a single-center retrospective pre-post cohort study conducted at Cooper University Hospital.
The TBW cohort was screened from July 1 through September 30, 2019, and the AdjBW cohort from July 1 through September 30, 2021.
Eligible patients were adults aged at least 18 years with suspected or confirmed VTE who received the standardized UFH infusion protocol for at least 24 hours without non-protocol interruption.

population.label: Adults with suspected or confirmed VTE receiving protocolized UFH
inclusion_criteria: UFH infusion through standardized protocol for at least 24 hours without non-protocol interruption

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients had to meet at least one target-population criterion: age at least 65 years and/or total body weight at least 100 kg.

population.label: Target older-adult and/or higher-body-weight population
inclusion_criteria: Age ≥65 years and/or total body weight ≥100 kg

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were required to have at least one anti-Xa level obtained six hours after UFH initiation.

population.label: Eligible UFH-treated patients
inclusion_criteria: At least one anti-Xa level six hours after UFH initiation

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for oral factor Xa inhibitor use during or directly before the index admission prior to UFH initiation.

population.label: Screened patients
exclusion_criteria: Oral factor Xa inhibitor during or directly prior to the index admission before UFH initiation

atoms.canonical_statement: Pregnant or actively incarcerated patients and patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation during UFH infusion were excluded.

population.label: Screened patients
exclusion_criteria: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation during UFH infusion

atoms.canonical_statement: Significant deviations from the institutional heparin protocol were exclusionary, including mistimed anti-Xa sampling, non-protocol rate changes, incorrect dosing weight, a starting rate other than 18 units/kg/hr, or a substantially incorrect initial 80-units/kg bolus.

population.label: Screened patients
exclusion_criteria: Significant variation from the approved institutional heparin protocol

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with missing height or height at or below 152.4 cm were excluded.
In the post-period, UFH was initiated at 18 units/kg/hr using adjusted body weight in patients meeting the age and/or weight criteria.

exposures.details: Initiation weight scalar: adjusted body weight; bolus use was at provider discretion.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the pre-period, UFH was initiated at 18 units/kg/hr using total body weight.

exposures.details: Initiation weight scalar: total body weight; bolus use was at provider discretion.

atoms.canonical_statement: Initial and adjustment bolus doses were permitted according to the institutional protocol at provider discretion.
Anti-Xa was measured six hours after UFH initiation and after rate changes, with weight-based rate adjustment to target 0.3 to 0.7 units/mL.
Anti-Xa was checked every six hours until two consecutive therapeutic levels, then every 24 hours until UFH discontinuation or a subsequent nontherapeutic level.
The primary endpoint was time to first therapeutic anti-Xa level, with the therapeutic range defined as 0.3 to 0.7 units/mL.

concept.text: Time to first therapeutic anti-Xa level

outcome.definition: Time from UFH initiation to first anti-Xa level within 0.3–0.7 units/mL

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary endpoints included whether the first measured anti-Xa was therapeutic and the proportion of therapeutic anti-Xa values during the first 24 hours.

concept.text: Therapeutic anti-Xa values within first 24 hours

outcome.definition: Proportion of measured anti-Xa values within the therapeutic range during the first 24 hours after UFH initiation

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety endpoints were in-hospital mortality and ISTH-defined major bleeding.

outcome.definition: ISTH major bleeding: overt bleeding with hemoglobin decrease ≥2 g/dL, transfusion of ≥2 units of whole blood/red cells, critical-site bleeding, or bleeding contributing to death

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary endpoint was analyzed with the Mann-Whitney U test, and the Hodges-Lehmann estimator was used to estimate the difference between population medians.
Secondary endpoints were analyzed with Pearson chi-square or Fisher exact testing for low-frequency outcomes.

Prespecified subgroup analyses evaluated patients weighing at least 100 kg, patients aged at least 65 years, and patients meeting both criteria; a post-hoc analysis compared patients with versus without an initial 80-units/kg bolus.
Of 571 screened patients, 90 met eligibility criteria and 10 were randomly excluded to balance the age and weight strata, leaving 80 patients for analysis.
Each treatment cohort contained 40 patients.
In each cohort, 27 patients (67.5%) were aged at least 65 years and weighed less than 100 kg.

population.label: Age ≥65 years only stratum across both cohorts

atoms.canonical_statement: In each cohort, 11 patients (27.5%) weighed at least 100 kg and were younger than 65 years.

population.label: Weight ≥100 kg only stratum across both cohorts

atoms.canonical_statement: In each cohort, 2 patients (5%) met both the age-at-least-65-years and weight-at-least-100-kg criteria.

population.label: Patients meeting both age and weight criteria across both cohorts

atoms.canonical_statement: Thirteen patients (32.5%) in each cohort received an initial 80-units/kg bolus.

population.label: Patients receiving initial 80-units/kg bolus across both cohorts

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean age was 68.8 years in the TBW cohort and 67.3 years in the AdjBW cohort (p=0.64).
Mean total body weight was 91.02 kg in the TBW cohort and 84.76 kg in the AdjBW cohort (p=0.33).
Concomitant antithrombotic medication use was more frequent in the AdjBW cohort than in the TBW cohort: 34/40 (85%) versus 25/40 (62.5%), p=0.02.

atoms.canonical_statement: The retrospective single-center design limits causal inference and generalizability.
Institution-specific UFH monitoring and titration protocols may limit applicability to other hospitals.
Anti-Xa samples drawn more than six hours after initiation or a rate change were retained; two patients in each cohort had a first anti-Xa level collected more than 10 hours after UFH initiation.

Hemolyzed samples required redraws in 12/249 TBW samples and 10/259 AdjBW samples and may have delayed time to therapeutic anti-Xa for five TBW patients and three AdjBW patients who had not yet reached goal.
The primary outcome was a laboratory surrogate rather than a patient-centered endpoint such as successful VTE treatment or reduced bleeding.
The study periods were chosen to avoid the early COVID-19 era, limiting generalizability to patients with COVID-19-associated coagulopathy.
The weight-only subgroup included only 11 patients per cohort and was considered likely underpowered to detect a difference.
Exclusion of 44 patients exposed to oral factor Xa inhibitors before UFH initiation limits direct applicability to patients transitioning from agents such as apixaban or rivaroxaban.
The authors concluded that AdjBW-based UFH initiation was associated with shorter time to therapeutic anti-Xa in the combined older-adult/higher-weight population.
The observed improvement in time to therapeutic anti-Xa was primarily seen in older adults.
The subgroup analysis did not find a statistically significant difference in time to therapeutic anti-Xa among higher-body-weight patients who were younger than 65 years.
The authors stated that larger prospective randomized studies are needed to determine clinical efficacy and bleeding effects of AdjBW-based UFH dosing.
The authors reported no organizational funding for the submitted work.
The authors reported no relevant financial or non-financial conflicts of interest.
Study data are not publicly available because of participant privacy; de-identified data may be requested from the corresponding author subject to IRB approval and data-use requirements.
The institutional review boards of Cooper University Hospital and Saint Joseph’s University granted a waiver of ethical approval for this retrospective study using clinical data.

source_internal_inconsistencies.location: Results narrative vs Table 2, journal p. 424
source_internal_inconsistencies.issue: First-24-hour therapeutic anti-Xa results differ: narrative reports 53% AdjBW vs 40% TBW, p=0.02; Table 2 reports 59/105 (56.2%) AdjBW vs 40/103 (38.8%) TBW, p=0.01.
source_internal_inconsistencies.handling: Both directly reported assertions were retained as separate atoms and tagged source_internal_inconsistency; no reconciliation was invented.

extraction_limitations: Online Resource 1 (full titration protocol) and Online Resource 2 (individual major bleeding event descriptions) were referenced by the article but were not included in the uploaded PDF; details unique to those supplements were not invented.
The main article states that the post-period used adjusted body weight but does not provide the exact adjusted-body-weight formula in the accessible main text; no formula was inferred.

Figure 2 provides directional and p-value information for subtherapeutic/therapeutic/supratherapeutic first anti-Xa categories, but exact bar percentages are not text-labeled in the accessible figure; exact unreported percentages were not estimated from bar heights.
Atoms are machine-extracted and marked needs_review rather than verified; no human source verification is represented.
